chunks: Ali narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
Indeed, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would detain in a blood accusation for six days; then if the heirs of the slain came with proof, otherwise he would let him go free.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءُ: the legal heirs or claimants of the slain person
key_terms.الدَّمِ: bloodshed, meaning a case involving killing
key_terms.بِثَبَتٍ: with established proof or confirming evidence
key_terms.خَلَّى سَبِيلَهُ: he released him and let him go

ai.seo_question: How long could a person be detained in a murder accusation if no proof was yet presented?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a judicial practice of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in cases involving accusation of bloodshed. It indicates a limited period of detention while awaiting proof from the heirs of the victim, after which the accused would be released if no evidence was produced.
